_comment: Guided tour of Excitation Windows. Targets are item_rects names of the app and of the shared review panel.

steps.title: Start with an example
steps.text: Load example writes a simulated two-colour PIE measurement (32 ps channels, donor pulse at 2 ns, acceptor pulse at 52 ns) into the workspace and detects its windows. Your own measurements come from the workspace list above it.

steps.title: What the data shows
steps.text: The plot shows the micro-time decay of every detector. Each excitation pulse is a rising edge; the detected window edges are drawn in orange, the current ones in grey.

steps.title: Detected and current windows
steps.text: The table lists each window: the current one (from the setup, converted to the data's channel width), the detected one in channels and nanoseconds, and which excitation it holds. prompt is the donor's pulse, delayed the acceptor's.

steps.title: Check a setup
steps.text: Pick a detector setup to hold its windows against the data. A setup made for another TCSPC (another channel width or range) is converted and flagged; a window that misses a pulse, cuts one or mixes two is reported.

steps.title: You decide
steps.text: Use detected windows saves the setup with the detected windows into the workspace; nothing changes before. A donor-only measurement shows one pulse only: windows cannot be placed from it, and the button stays off.

await.hint: Press Use detected windows, or skip.
